tasks.short: Inspect and test equipment, judge whether continued operation is hazardous, and advise management in person and in writing.

steps.what: Electrician inspects the installation and measures insulation, earthing and RCD trips
Electrician compares findings with the standard and judges whether operation is hazardous
Electrician tells the client's management about the hazard on the spot
Electrician writes the findings and advice report with photos

loop.input: The electrician's voice note on each finding, with the uploaded measurements and photos.
loop.output: Defect fields per finding (location, circuit, defect code, severity) and a short draft remark.
loop.check: Defect codes must come from the fixed defect list, severity must fit the code and measured values must equal the uploaded results. The electrician reads each defect and advice line against the voice note, the photo and the measurement: the photo must show the defect and the code must describe what was found; unclear lines are written by hand.
loop.stop: One pass per note; unclear findings stay empty for the electrician to fill.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings are spoken in free text on site; a form alone means typing with gloves on.

steps.what: Electrician checks and signs the final report: defects, severity and advice say what was found and judged on site, and it goes to the client's facility manager
Electrician sends the signed report to the client: by e-mail today, by one send from the inspection module after the change
Client's facility manager decides to stop, repair or accept with measures
Electrician locks out the equipment when the client decides to stop it

tasks.design: Test instrument results upload into the inspection module of the installer's {ERP} or site app, a voice note becomes defect fields from the fixed defect list, and the advice report is generated from measurements, defects and photos. The electrician checks and signs the report before it goes to the client; the hazard judgement and the conversation stay with the electrician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were copied by hand from the tester, and reports were typed in the evening.
tasks.enabler_now: Site apps keep checklists, defects and photos and build reports; testers export measurements.
tasks.still_hard: Judging hazard and persuading a client to stop equipment are the job; defect lists must match the standard in use.
tasks.human_edge: Judging real risk on site and saying clearly to management that equipment must stop.

ambition.what: Clients see every open defect and its severity on their installation between inspections, not only in a yearly report.

tasks.altitude: The electrician signs generated reports instead of writing them; advice and lock-out decisions stay as they are.

reach.task: Report unsafe equipment to the facility manager
reach.learn: Whether the same defect list and photo report work for general maintenance.

evidence.claim: Construction software keeps site diaries, defect logs, checklists and handover reports.
One project manager reports saving about 10 hours a week on site diaries, defects and acceptance with such software (self-reported, vendor-published).
Employers must keep up-to-date diagrams of every electrical installation, and hazardous electrical work is limited to expert, instructed and authorised workers.
Building installations must meet the national installation standard.

assumptions: Boundary: from inspection to the client's decision and lock-out; repair work is outside.
Input contract: measurements exported by the test instrument; defect code list kept by the company's quality lead from the inspection standard; photos taken in the app; fallback is a typed report.
Client time is outside the electrician's savings.

Inspection, judgement, the conversation and signing the report keep their full time. s4 keeps 40 because measurements and codes fill in, but the electrician reads every line against the notes and photos. s7 keeps 20 for the send.
unknowns: Whether the company's test instruments export to the app.
How many inspections with advice an electrician does per month.
research_questions: Do clients act faster on defects shown in a live list than in a yearly report?

already_counted.description: Electrician checks the generated report and defect codes before signing.

incremental.description: Electrician fixes failed tester uploads and unclear voice notes.
Quality lead keeps the defect code list aligned with the standard.

approvals.approved_version: The signed inspection report with measurements, defects, photos and advice exactly as checked by the electrician in s4c, sent once to the client's facility manager; any change needs a new check and signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: inspections with many unusual findings, where much advice text is still written by hand (7.0); high: routine inspections with standard defects (12.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit the site, sketch the electrical layout and prepare a cost estimate for materials and labour.

steps.what: Electrician visits the site and discusses the client's wishes
Electrician measures and draws preliminary sketches of outlets, circuits and cable routes
Electrician lists materials and hours for the cost estimates in a spreadsheet
Electrician looks up material prices in the wholesaler's catalogue
Project leader checks the generated quote: scope, quantities, prices and margin, and the client it goes to, and approves it
Electrician sends the approved quote to the client: by e-mail today, by one send from the estimating module after the change
Electrician answers the client's questions and prepares revisions, which go back through the project leader's check before they are sent

tasks.design: The electrician sketches on a tablet with electrical symbols; the symbol count feeds the estimating module of the installer's {ERP}, where assemblies (an outlet with box, cable and labour time) turn counts into materials and hours priced from the sector's product data on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The quote is generated from the estimate; the project leader checks it with the margin and approves it, the electrician sends it, and revisions reuse the same estimate and go through the same check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sketches were on paper and estimates rebuilt line by line in spreadsheets with prices looked up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Installer ERPs and the sector's shared product and price data make assembly-based estimates a configuration job.
tasks.still_hard: Existing buildings hide surprises; a sketch on site still needs an experienced eye for routes and capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what the client really wants and seeing the practical cable route in an old building.

ambition.what: Quotes sent the day after the site visit, so fewer jobs are lost to slower competitors.

tasks.altitude: The electrician sketches and checks; arithmetic and price lookups disappear. Pricing rights stay with the project leader.

reach.learn: Whether assemblies work as well for piping as for wiring.

evidence.claim: A Dutch product and price data hub for the installation sector feeds installer software.
An ERP for installation firms handles work orders and material ordering.
Quotes to consumers must show prices including VAT; consumer protection details follow national rules.
Building installations must meet the national installation standard, which the design must respect.

assumptions: Boundary: from the site visit to the quote accepted or revised; the installation work is outside.

Input contract: assembly library with materials and labour per assembly, kept by the estimator in the {ERP}; prices from the sector data feed; symbol set for the tablet sketch; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Project leader and client time is outside the electrician's savings.

The site visit keeps its full time. s3 keeps 40 for checking generated quantities and adding one-off items. s6 keeps 20 for the send. s7 keeps 80 because questions are still answered by the electrician.
unknowns: Whether the company has an assembly library.
How many quotes an electrician prepares per month.
research_questions: Does faster quoting raise the share of quotes accepted?

already_counted.description: Electrician checks the assembly quantities generated from the sketch.

incremental.description: Electrician adds missing assemblies and reports wrong labour times.
Estimator keeps assemblies and labour norms current.

approvals.approved_version: The quote with scope, quantities, prices and margin exactly as approved by the project leader in s5, sent once to the client named on the request; any revision needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: renovations with many one-off items outside the assemblies, so quantities and prices are still worked out by hand for many lines (21.1); high: standard work covered by assemblies (35.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep work order records and client files, prepare weekly reports and order supplies for the van.

steps.what: Electrician fills in the work order with hours worked, materials used and work done: on paper today; in the app after the change, with materials from scans and tester results attached
Client signs the work order on the electrician's phone
Electrician checks the closed work order before it goes to invoicing: hours, materials and work done match the job, and the client's signature is there
Electrician files test reports and installation drawings in the client's records
Electrician prepares reports of jobs done and open items for the project leader
Electrician checks the weekly report: jobs done and open items match the work orders, and the remarks say what is meant
Electrician sends the checked weekly report to the project leader
Electrician checks van stock
Electrician checks the replenishment order: articles and quantities fit the van's shortfall, and the wholesaler and delivery point are right
Electrician releases the checked order to the wholesaler: typed in today, one release of the proposal after the change
The work order goes to the ERP for invoicing: typed in by the office administrator today, posted from the closed work order after the change
Project leader reviews the weekly report and open items

tasks.design: Configure the work order app of the installer's {ERP}: hours, scanned van-stock materials, photos, the client's signature and tester results go on the work order, and drawings and test reports attach to the client's file in {DOCS}. The electrician checks each closed work order before it goes to invoicing. Weekly reports come from closed work orders and the electrician checks and sends them, and a van-stock list with minimums proposes replenishment orders that the electrician checks and releases to the wholesaler.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper work orders were retyped by the office, and van stock was checked by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Installer ERPs capture hours and materials on site and order electronically; a case showed handhelds replacing paper work orders with higher output.
tasks.still_hard: Electricians must log materials as they use them; logs per worker raise works council and privacy questions.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the next jobs will need in the van and keeping client files honest and complete.

ambition.what: Jobs invoiced the day they close instead of at month end.

tasks.altitude: The electrician confirms records and orders instead of writing them twice; reporting decisions move to the project leader's dashboard.

reach.task: Keep installation records and order panels and parts
reach.learn: Whether the same work order app covers PV installation records.

evidence.claim: An ERP for installation firms captures work orders, hours and materials on site and handles material ordering and call-off.
About 200 handhelds replaced paper work orders at a sewer cleaning firm; orders per day rose from about 1,550 to 2,000 with payback in six months (director's figures, 2009).
Up-to-date diagrams of every electrical installation are required.
Hours, location and job logs per fitter observe presence and performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from closing a job to records filed, reported and supplies ordered; invoicing itself is outside.
Input contract: van-stock list with minimums set by the warehouse manager; article codes scanned from van stock; tester results exported from the instrument; fallback is the paper work order.
No van location tracking is added.
Office, client and project leader time, including the client's signature (s1k, share 1), is outside the electrician's savings.

s1 keeps 80 because hours and work done are still written by the electrician; only writing article codes and copying test values goes. The three checks keep their full time; s7 keeps 20 for the release.
unknowns: Whether the company's ERP has a mobile work order app.
How van stock is replenished today.
research_questions: How many days pass between job completion and invoice today?

already_counted.description: Electrician checks the generated weekly report and adds remarks.
Electrician confirms or edits the replenishment proposal.

incremental.description: Electrician scans materials as used and corrects missed scans.
Warehouse manager keeps van-stock lists and minimums current.

approvals.approved_version: The replenishment order with articles and quantities exactly as checked by the electrician in s4c, sent once to the wholesaler for delivery to the van's pick-up point; any change needs a new check.
The closed work order with hours, materials, work done and the client's signature exactly as checked by the electrician in s1c, posted once to the {ERP} for invoicing; any change reopens the check.
The weekly report of jobs done and open items exactly as checked by the electrician in s3c, sent once to the project leader in the {ERP}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: electricians log materials late or partly, so work orders are completed by hand and reports need much rework (41.3); high: materials scanned as used (49.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The electrician keeps testing, judging hazards, sketching and the client conversation; reports, estimates and records are generated and checked.
skills_to_grow: Recording findings and materials precisely in the app
role.ambitious_version: An electrician who quotes the next day, closes jobs with complete files and invoices, and gives clients a live view of open defects.
